A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FDS research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, algorithms and appendices are readable and can be matched across revisions, including the renumbered appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments, image-generation benchmarks, inverse-problem results and ablations in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds surrogate-agreement measurements, further generation comparisons and a 44-participant user study.

M1.justification: The refinement equations and both algorithms are unchanged. However, v1 restricts FDS to early timesteps, whereas v2 Section 3.2 says to deactivate it there; v2 Section 6.2 still specifies early refinement. The PDFs do not resolve whether this reflects an actual timing change or a wording error.

E1.justification: v2 adds MS-COCO text-to-image evaluation and human preference assessment of existing generation tasks. The checkerboard, CIFAR-10, ImageNet, DrawBench and Cat coverage remains. Additional backbones and solvers expand configurations rather than generation task families.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons with UniPC, RK4 and CFG-Zero*, each with and without FDS, in Table 4. FLUX.1 and SD3.5-M also become evaluated text-to-image baselines. UniPC was previously cited but not evaluated; the original comparator sets remain elsewhere.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include ordering agreement over 50K sampled pairs and a 44-participant study using 20 ImageNet, 20 text-to-image and 10 inverse-problem pairs. v2 also introduces UniPC at 20 NFEs, additional backbone configurations and MS-COCO FID/CLIP evaluation at CFG 3 and 7. These are additional protocols, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's visual comparison of synthetic discrepancy maps, v2 Appendix D quantitatively tests surrogate ordering on checkerboard and CIFAR-10 data. Appendix E.1 adds human assessment of perceptual improvements, and Table 4 tests compatibility with advanced inference methods. The original truncation, perturbation-schedule, iteration and candidate-count ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 64 independent repetitions for timing measurements. v2 adds point estimates of agreement and human preferences but no confidence intervals, significance tests or new seed-based uncertainty reporting. Calling the user-study improvements significant does not document a statistical test.

E6.justification: v2 adds FLUX.1, SD3.5-M, advanced inference-method and MS-COCO results, agreement rates of 89.82% and 82.19%, and a reported average human win rate of 72.9%. Original main, inverse-problem, 100-step and SiT scores remain unchanged. DrawBench's CFG 3 result block is removed; its CFG 7 values are retained with equivalent rounding. Added comparisons are mixed across metrics: for example, FLUX.1 aesthetic score decreases from 6.18 to 6.14 with FDS.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 39 newly defines the pairwise ordering-agreement probability used in the surrogate analysis. The central theorem, assumptions, lemmas and complete Appendix A proof are unchanged; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: divergence characterizes velocity discrepancy, FDS provides training-free spatial refinement, and it improves generation across backbones, solvers and tasks. The new experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly acknowledges approximately 18% ordering errors on CIFAR-10 and argues that local perturbations limit harmful trajectory deviations. v2 also interprets the user study and MS-COCO results as evidence for perceptual quality and generalization. Existing explanations of early-stage benefits, capacity bottlenecks and pixel-versus-latent behavior are retained.

D1.justification: The project URL and most Appendix C implementation information remain unchanged. However, v2 removes the guidance-scale label from retained DrawBench Table 2 values and removes the CFG 3/7 captions from unchanged qualitative examples, formerly Figure 12 and now Figure 13. This reduces configuration traceability.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Black Forest Labs/FLUX.1, CFG-Zero* and MS-COCO. The related-work discussion and positioning against training-based crossing methods, numerical solvers and externally guided refinement remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language edits, expands the intuitive introduction to Section 3.1, adds author and funding information, and organizes additional experiments into appendix subsections. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact rather than undergoing an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4, 7, 10 and 11 and the user-study chart, restructures Table 2 by backbone, and expands Figure 4 with FLUX.1 examples. It also changes to US-letter pages with substantially wider margins and revises several captions and table headers. Existing appendix image grids are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The CIFAR-10 surrogate check and human study strengthen support for reliability and perceptual quality beyond v1's synthetic illustrations and automatic metrics. Advanced-method and MS-COCO evaluations further support the existing applicability claims. These gains are moderated by the new contradiction about early-stage activation and the removal of DrawBench guidance-scale results and labels, leaving a limited net improvement in evidential quality.
